statement: GET /api/orders?q=Alice returns every order, ignoring the query filter.
Filtering orders by customer name actually searches the item field, so a name query returns nothing.
GET /api/orders/1004 returns the Standing desk order (id 1001) instead of the Webcam order that was actually requested.
GET /api/orders/1002 returns order 1001 (the previous order) instead of 1002.
Requesting a nonexistent order id returns 200 with an empty object instead of a 404 error.
Filtering by "alice" (lowercase) finds nothing because the match is now case-sensitive.
A search query with a leading space (" Alice") never matches, though "Alice" would.
GET /api/orders returns 404 Not Found; the route was renamed to /api/order without updating clients.
GET /api/orders/1001 returns 404; the single-order endpoint's path was capitalized in a code change.
GET /api/orders/1001 returns 404 not found for every id because the id is now compared as text instead of a number.
GET /api/orders (with no search box filled in) fails with a 422 error instead of showing all orders.
The orders list comes back sorted by price, highest first, instead of the original order.
The two newest orders (Chidi Okafor's webcam and Dana Whitfield's headset) never show up; the deployed server is running an older snapshot of the order data.
No matter what you search for, /api/orders only ever returns Alice Nguyen's orders.
Requesting a negative or zero order id crashes the server with an unhandled error instead of returning a clean 404.

category: works in dev but not on the production build
statement: Search filtering on /api/orders only works when a DEBUG environment variable is set; in a normal (production) deployment every search returns the full list.
Opening a single order's detail (GET /api/orders/1001) shows a total twice the real price.
The health check endpoint returns an empty object instead of {"status": "ok"}, so uptime monitors can't confirm the service is healthy.
GET /api/orders always returns an empty list; a leftover duplicate route registered earlier shadows the real handler.
Searching for "Alice" returns every order except Alice's; the match condition was inverted.
The pinned FastAPI version in requirements.txt is years out of date and fails to install/import in the current environment, so the service never starts.
The whole API fails to start: even GET /health returns nothing because the server process can't boot due to a code error.
GET /api/orders/1001 always returns 404 Not Found; the lookup compares the id against the customer name field by mistake.
When a search matches nothing, /api/orders returns an object {"orders": []} instead of an empty array, breaking clients that expect a list.
A single order's detail view shows the price under the key "amount" instead of "total", and after the first request the price disappears from that order everywhere.
Searching for a customer with multiple orders always leaves out the last one in the results.
Every single-order detail page shows the item name as "Sample Item" instead of the real product.
Typing part of a name, like "nguyen", returns no results; only an exact full-name match works now.
GET /api/orders/1001 (no trailing slash) returns 404; the route now requires a trailing slash that the app's own links don't include.
Searching for a customer with zero matching orders crashes the endpoint with a division-by-zero error instead of returning an empty list.
The single-order detail endpoint returns a one-item array instead of the order object itself, breaking any client expecting a single record.
Loading the orders page normally (no search text) shows an empty list instead of every order; only typing something makes any orders appear.
